nodes.label: Hand Mode (MediaPipe Hand Landmarker gestures)
nodes.rationale: Uses a plain webcam with 21 joints per hand in-browser; pinch to drag, two-hand pinch rotate/scale, fist deselect, both palms calculate. Joints sent to server twice a second for occlusion check.

nodes.label: import_mesh with Vertex-Clustering Decimation
nodes.rationale: Imported GLB meshes are decimated to ~4,000 triangles and scaled to ~80 mm so they cannot overload the optics; UV unwrapping skipped since holograms use single laser colour without textures.

nodes.label: Text-to-CAD (build_assembly part library)
nodes.rationale: Muse Spark writes assemblies as JSON from a parametric library (gear, tube, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, box, nozzle, coil, blade ring, pipe); server validates and reports rejected parts back so the model can fix them. Results are simplified parametric models, not manufacturer data.

nodes.label: Omitted Features (node material editor, WebXR, Meshy/Luma)
nodes.norm_label: omitted features (node material editor, webxr, meshy/luma)
nodes.rationale: Node editor adds UI without changing single-colour laser physics; WebXR contradicts the no-headset goal; Meshy/Luma are paid and not Meta tooling, but import_mesh accepts their GLB output.

nodes.label: One State, Three Ways to Edit (shared tools)
nodes.norm_label: one state, three ways to edit (shared tools)
nodes.rationale: Laptop gizmo, hand controller and AI agent all call the same tools (add_part, update_part, build_assembly) on server-owned state.parts, so mode switching (Tab) is instant and lossless; undo/redo snapshots parts and restores via /api/scene.

nodes.label: Single Geometry Source (Python builds meshes)
nodes.rationale: engine/geometry.py builds every mesh and the browser only draws /api/meshes, so the picture shown equals the geometry the physics engine uses.

nodes.label: Hologram and Eye-View Reconstruction Panels with Focus Sweep
nodes.norm_label: hologram and eye-view reconstruction panels with focus sweep

nodes.label: Hand-Shadow Rule / Depth Conflict (hand_check)
nodes.rationale: A hand on the panel-to-P segment blocks light that should appear in front of the hand: a depth conflict software cannot fix; a hand on P-to-eye is ordinary occlusion.

nodes.label: Speckle Analysis (sparse point groups)
nodes.rationale: At k=3 contrast drops 0.995 -> 0.358 (random frames) and 0.288 (sparse groups), still far above the ~0.03-0.04 visible threshold, so speckle is reported honestly as an open problem.

nodes.label: Wavefront Recording Plane (multi-plane WRP)
nodes.rationale: Points cut into 1.5 mm depth slabs written to nearby planes so windows are tiny, then propagated by angular spectrum; 5x faster than direct and focuses better.

nodes.label: Sharp Zone (+/-100 mm of panel)
nodes.rationale: Within +/-100 mm the desk keeps 78-90% of full sharpness; floating at 25 cm would need kHz phase modulators which do not exist yet.

nodes.label: Two Scales (lab-scale SLM vs desk-scale geometric laws)
nodes.norm_label: two scales (lab-scale slm vs desk-scale geometric laws)
nodes.rationale: A 27-inch hologram needs ~3e7 pixels at 45 um, so full wave simulation runs on a 1024^2 x 8 um lab SLM with the scene shrunk uniformly; desk-scale questions use geometric laws and the eye model.
